about: Tests of the previous release that fail by design when its database job runs against this release's schema (OPS-008; docs/architecture/rollback.md), in two ways that are not what the release does: the test checks the schema itself, or it sets itself up by writing rows straight into the database in a shape the release's own code never writes, which a guard this schema adds refuses. Each entry names the migrations that cause it, one test file, the tests of that file that fail for that reason, each by its full name, and why the previous release still runs. An entry is read only while one of its migrations is new to the previous release. Any other failure fails the rollback job, and so does a listed test that does not fail.

tests: the money, drafting assistant and whole-workspace readings count every workspace's rows of the last hour, and no older one
failures.reason: The test writes its checkouts straight into the database, each at an amount its one price does not give, to count the money of the last hour, so it stops before it reads anything. The guard that 20261127172934_order_price_book_guard adds refuses an order whose amount, line or price in effect is not its price's own (PAY-001), by design. The previous release's own code never writes such an order: its createOrder and its bundle order take the amount, currency and line from the price or the bundle in effect, which is what the guard requires.

tests: another workspace's identifiers are refused exactly like unknown ones and change nothing
failures.reason: The test writes orders straight into the database to set up its cases, with an amount and line their price does not give, so it stops before its cases run. The guard that 20261127172934_order_price_book_guard adds refuses an order whose amount, line or price in effect is not its price's own (PAY-001), by design. The previous release's own code never writes such an order: its createOrder and its bundle order take the amount, currency and line from the price or the bundle in effect, which is what the guard requires. Were its orders their prices' own, its list of the tables row-level security limits to one workspace would still differ from the database's, which 20261127001808_message_deliveries and 20261127033059_notice_digests lengthen with two tables the previous release never reads or writes.

tests: the release record names the commit, the migrations shipped and applied, every content and rule version and the known issues
failures.reason: The test checks the release record against the database it runs on, and requires the migrations the release ships and those the database has applied to match. Here the database has applied this release's new migrations as well, so the record says, truly, that they do not match. It checks the schema itself, not what the release does.
